what: Direct checks of P2 row 1, P2 (i), P2 (iii) and README row 2's plugin-arm byte clause against the registered text. coding.json is kept exactly as code_rows.py produced it; code_rows.py is not modified.
ruling: Owner's Ruling 2, 2026-11-16: P2 HOLDS, 4 of 4, under the registered text. Row 1 and (i) met. (iii) met under the definition the plugin itself committed before P2 in ad22de4 (tagged bytes are a prefix of the new bytes; the separator belongs to the append), applied identically to README row 2. Row 3 FAIL stands as genuine.
disclosure: The literal reading of (iii) fails by one separator byte (975 vs 974); under it P2 is 3 of 4 and the forecast is FALSIFIED, and README row 2 for the plugin arm would read 'no'. The registration's wording should have said 'prefix' and will in any v0.3.
coder_defects: 1. Row 1 / P2 (i), two causes: commits are found by parsing the '[branch hash] message' line `git commit` prints, and `git commit -q` prints none, so the pre-registration commit was not seen; and the text `python3 calc.py` inside the heredoc body that wrote the prediction file (its **Check:** line) was counted as an execution of calc.py.
2. P2 (iii): exact equality of the bytes above `## Outcome` with the tagged file, where the plugin's committed definition is a prefix test; the append's separator newline made it fail.

3. Row 6: the oracle's exit code and stderr are ignored, so an oracle that does not run reads as 0 dead links (found when a relative oracle path was passed; all codings were re-run with absolute paths).
coder_gap_found_applying_the_ruling: Row 2's code does not test the plugin-arm byte clause at all (it checks that the lines stating 42 survive). The (iii) direct check below covers that clause on the same T2 snapshot.
